title: How Far Should Leaders Go to Accommodate a Superstar
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article addresses how leaders should treat their highest-performing team members without undermining team cohesion. It grants that special treatment — extra time, resources, attention — is appropriate for superstars, but draws three firm boundaries: superstars must be held to the same rules as everyone else, must still receive honest feedback and evaluation, and must never be excused from team activities. The argument is that violating any of these three boundaries, rather than the extra attention itself, is what destroys team morale, since other members are watching closely to see whether special talent buys exemption from the norms that bind everyone else.
points: Special treatment for top performers is endorsed as legitimate, but bounded by three specific non-negotiables: equal rules, unsoftened feedback, and mandatory participation.
The morale-destroying trigger isn't giving a superstar extra resources — it's exempting them from rules, feedback, or team activities that bind everyone else.
The article frames this as a visible test the whole team watches: exemptions granted to a superstar signal what the leader actually values, regardless of what's said.
quotes: Leaders naturally treat their best team members differently than others. They give them more time, attention, responsibility, and information.
Special treatment for the Superstar does not undermine the goodwill and collaborative spirit of the team…as long as three issues are excluded from this distinctive approach.
First and foremost, Superstars must be held to the same standards and rules as everyone else.
Second, the Superstar is not spared from the feedback and evaluations everyone else receives.
No matter how extraordinary a Superstar might be, the team must always matter more. Good leaders don’t turn Superstars into stupid stars.
